ctenosuchus:study:1.title: A new teleosauroid (Crocodylomorpha, Thalattosuchia) with a unique dentition from the Middle Jurassic of eastern Morocco (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Ctenosuchus is classified as a member of the family Teleosauridae.
facts.quote: A member of the family Teleosauridae.

facts.statement: The type locality for Ctenosuchus is the Anoual Formation.
Ctenosuchus fossils have been found in Morocco.
Ctenosuchus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age.
Ctenosuchus was described by Imran and colleagues.
Ctenosuchus is a newly described genus and species.
The genus Ctenosuchus was established by Imran et al. in 2026.
Ctenosuchus is known from two specimens that preserve partial skulls and osteoderms.
facts.quote: known from two specimens, both of which preserve partial skulls and osteoderms.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the interlocking teeth of Ctenosuchus were an adaptation for trapping prey like small crustaceans, fish, and soft-bodied animals.
facts.quote: The interlocking teeth of Ctenosuchus may have been an adaptation for trapping prey, such as small crustaceans, fish, and soft-bodied animals.

facts.statement: The study describing Ctenosuchus was authored by Hamzah Imran, David M. Martill, Roy E. Smith, Samir Zouhri, James Gunn, and Nizar Ibrahim.
facts.quote: Authors: Hamzah Imran, David M. Martill, Roy E. Smith, Samir Zouhri, James Gunn, Nizar Ibrahim

facts.statement: The description of Ctenosuchus was published in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

rejected.statement: Ctenosuchus is characterized by a unique arrangement of widely spaced, needle-like teeth.
rejected.quote: It is characterized by a unique arrangement of widely spaced, needle-like teeth unlike those of all other known crocodylomorphs.
